title: Bright River Solar
tagline: A 50 MWp solar plant in Vietnam. The sponsor wants a term sheet by Friday.
tutorialHint: Always check the sponsor's numbers against the independent engineer.

head: Item
Detail
rows: Bright River Solar, 50 MWp ground-mounted solar plant
Lotus Peak Renewables Pte. Ltd. (Singapore). Operates two solar plants in Thailand, 30 MWp in total
Construction starts Q1 2027, commercial operation Q1 2028
15 years after commercial operation, annuity repayment
20 years, USD 7.0 cents/kWh, paid in VND at the daily exchange rate
Fixed-price, date-certain EPC contract with a tier-1 contractor, delay damages included

items: Minimum DSCR of 1.30x on the bank's P90 case
Debt service reserve account (DSRA) covering 6 months of debt service

head: Assumption
Value
rows: Cash flow available for debt service

blocks.text: Tax is ignored: the project benefits from a corporate tax holiday during its first years.

Ninh Thuan has the best sun in Vietnam. Our yield is based on our own satellite data and on the performance of our Thai plants. Grid connection is secured: the PPA is signed and the substation is only 4 km away.
We could not reconcile the sponsor's yield of 1,750 kWh/kWp with long-term irradiance data for the site. The Thai plants it refers to sit in a different climate zone and are not a valid comparison.

The 110 kV substation also serves four other solar plants totalling 350 MWp. Until the planned 220 kV line is in service (expected 2029, not yet funded), we expect EVN to curtail the plant's output by 8% to 12% per year. The standard EVN PPA does not compensate the plant for curtailed energy.

items: Plant design and EPC contractor: sound, no concerns.
Operating budget of USD 0.75m per year: reasonable.

onStart.text: Hi, quick one on Bright River. Lotus Peak wants a signed term sheet by Friday. Another bank is offering them 80% gearing, so our 75% is already a stretch. They're a key client for our renewables push in Vietnam. Please don't kill this one.

committeeClosing.text: Thank you. The committee will deliberate. You'll hear from us shortly.

decisions.label: Approve as requested
decisions.hint: Lend the amount requested, on the sponsor's terms.

decisions.label: Approve with conditions
decisions.hint: Change the amount and add conditions to protect the bank.

conditions.label: DSRA of 6 months funded at close
conditions.reason: Six months of debt service set aside in cash: a buffer for a bad year.

conditions.label: Cash sweep while curtailment > 5%
conditions.reason: Excess cash repays the loan faster while the grid is constrained.

conditions.label: Dividend lock-up below 1.15x DSCR
conditions.reason: Cash stays in the project instead of going to the sponsor when the DSCR falls.

conditions.label: Sponsor guarantee covering curtailment losses until the grid upgrade
conditions.reason: The only way to keep USD 28.5m: the sponsor covers the lost revenue until the 220 kV line.
conditions.redundantReason: Not needed once the loan is cut to the right size. It only adds weight for the sponsor.

conditions.label: Higher margin (+50 bp)
conditions.reason: More revenue for the bank, but a higher rate raises debt service and makes the DSCR worse.

conditions.label: Completion guarantee from the sponsor until commercial operation
conditions.reason: The fixed-price, date-certain EPC contract with delay damages already covers construction risk.

conditions.label: Second independent yield study before signing
conditions.reason: The independent engineer has already done it, and it would push signing past Friday.

committee.question: Which production number did you use to size the loan, and why?
committee.goodAnswer: The engineer's P90 (1,430 kWh/kWp), not the sponsor's 1,750. Lenders rely on the independent view.

committee.question: EVN can curtail this plant without paying. How is the bank protected?
committee.goodAnswer: A curtailment haircut in the bank case, debt sized at 1.30x on that case, plus sponsor support or a cash sweep until the grid upgrade. The DSRA as a buffer.

ideas.label: Curtailment haircut in the bank case
Sponsor support or cash sweep until the grid upgrade

committee.question: The client wants USD 28.5m and has an 80% offer elsewhere. Why can't we match it?
committee.goodAnswer: At USD 28.5m the DSCR is 1.20x, below policy. Offer USD 26m, or USD 28.5m with sponsor support. Stays firm but proposes a way to close.

committeeScale.2: Right idea backed by the numbers

competition.explain: Each condition, and any cut to the amount requested, weighs on the sponsor. Above 5, Lotus Peak takes the competitor's 80% offer.

right.label: Approve with the right conditions
right.story: Deal closes at USD 26m. Curtailment hits 11%, DSCR holds at about 1.30x. Kevin grumbles, the client signs.

approve.label: Approve as requested
approve.story: DSCR falls to 1.18x. Dividends are locked up and the loan goes on the watchlist.

weak.label: Approve with weak conditions
weak.story: Same watchlist outcome: the conditions don't fix the sizing. DSCR falls to 1.18x and the loan goes on the watchlist.

lost.label: Lost to competitor
lost.story: Your term sheet is too heavy for Lotus Peak. They sign with the competitor bank at 80% gearing. Kevin tells your boss you had a workable deal and over-structured it.

decline.label: Decline
decline.story: A competitor bank closes the deal. Kevin complains to your boss.

outcomeContext: The consequence appears two or three cases later, when 2028 curtailment comes in at 11%.

spotted: The sponsor's yield of 1,750 kWh/kWp is 22% above the independent engineer's P90 of 1,430. Banks size loans on the independent P90, not on the sponsor's figures.
The sponsor assumed no curtailment. The engineer expects 8% to 12% until a grid line that isn't funded yet, and the PPA doesn't pay for lost output.
debrief.summary: With both fixed, a USD 28.5m loan only reaches a 1.20x DSCR. The fix: cut the loan to about USD 26m, or ask the sponsor to cover curtailment losses until the grid upgrade.
debrief.lesson: When the numbers don't work, fix the structure before reaching for a refusal.

answerKey.summary: Once both traps are fixed, the requested USD 28.5m loan only reaches a 1.20x DSCR, below the bank's 1.30x minimum. The deal works at about USD 26m.

traps.title: Trap 1 — Inflated energy yield
traps.text: The sponsor uses 1,750 kWh/kWp, 22% above the independent engineer's P90 of 1,430 kWh/kWp. Lenders size debt on the independent P90, never on the sponsor's case.

traps.title: Trap 2 — Curtailment ignored
traps.text: The sponsor assumes 100% grid availability. The engineer expects 8% to 12% curtailment until a 220 kV line that is not yet funded, and the PPA does not pay for curtailed energy. The bank case uses 10%.

rightDecision.title: Right decision: approve with conditions
rightDecision.intro: At least one condition must fix the sizing:
options: Cut the loan to USD 26.0m (gearing 68%, DSCR 1.32x). Sponsor equity rises from USD 9.5m to USD 12.0m.
Or keep USD 28.5m only if the sponsor covers curtailment losses (guarantee or cash top-up) until the 220 kV line is in service.

answerKey.extraCredit: Conditions that earn extra credit: the 6-month DSRA funded at financial close (about USD 1.4m at USD 26m), a cash sweep while curtailment stays above 5%, a dividend lock-up below 1.15x DSCR.
answerKey.weakAnswers: Weak answers: a higher margin alone (it does not fix the cash flow), or matching the competitor's 80% gearing.
